summary: Herbert Härtel specialized in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1953–1986), directed the Museum of Asian Art (1963–1986), and taught at Freie Universität Berlin (1965–1986).

Herbert Niel Randle worked in Indology and philosophy. Around 1908 he was a professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and later served as Librarian for the India Office Records (1927–1949) and India Office (around 1933–1949).

Herbert V. Guenther worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Munich and Vienna, he also trained under traditional Tibetan teachers. He held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert Weir Smyth was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology. He studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. His academic posts included Bryn Mawr College (1887–1901) and Harvard University, starting as Eliot Professor in 1901.

Herbert Zachert was a Japanologist who studied under Karl Florenz between around 1928 and 1933. He later held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (around 1949–1960) and the University of Bonn (around 1960–1974).

Herman Kellgren worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. From around 1849 to 1856, he held a post at the University of Helsinki.

Hermann Beckh worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at the Royal Library of Berlin (1908–1916), Humboldt University (1911–1921), and the Kiel Institute for the World Economy.
Hermann Berger was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Helmut Hoffmann between around 1949 and 1953. He later held an academic post at Heidelberg University from around 1964 to 1992.
Hermann Beythan worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Raja Pillai.

Hermann Bonitz worked in philosophy. He studied at the University of Leipzig and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at the University of Vienna (around 1849–1867) and the Prussian Ministry of Spiritual, Educational and Medical Affairs (around 1875–1888).

Hermann Brockhaus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He became a professor at the University of Jena in 1839 and at the University of Leipzig from 1848 until 1877.

Hermann Brunnhofer worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Bonn, Berlin, Zurich, and under Albrecht Weber. He held positions at Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek (1881–1888), Saint Petersburg State University (1891–1901), and the University of Bern (1901–1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus around 1862–1865 and later served as a Gymnasialprofessor at Gymnasium Zwickau from around 1876 to 1904.

Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg under August Fick and Theodor Benfey. He held faculty posts at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg around 1875–1879. He later served as a professor at the University of Giessen from around 1904 to 1922.

Hermann Goetz worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Munich and under Jean Philippe Vogel. He curated the Baroda Museum (1939–1953), directed the National Gallery of Modern Art (1953), and directed art history at Heidelberg University (1961–1976).

Hermann Grassmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher and later taught at several institutions, serving for decades as a professor at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from around 1842 to 1877.

Hermann Güntert worked in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University from around 1912 to 1921 and at the University of Rostock from around 1921 to 1928.

Hermann Hirt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg and Leipzig. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Leipzig (1891–1912) before becoming a professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Giessen (1912–1936).

Hermann Hunger is an archaeologist and linguist who studied at Vienna, Heidelberg, and Münster. He held positions at the German Archaeological Institute (1964–1967), the University of Chicago (1970–1978), and the University of Vienna (1978–2007).
